newsitem.title: UK: UK shares close at highest level for five weeks.
newsitem.headline: UK shares close at highest level for five weeks.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 sets highest close for five weeks, taking lead from overnight surge on Wall St which lifts stocks across Europe.
** Dow firm as London trade ends, shaking off initial weakness.
** Barclays leads bank stocks higher, insurers also help drive market advance. ICI up ahead of Q1 results Thursday.

Yet the FTSE 100 failed to break through the 4,400 level and participants said the market could still find it difficult to make much more progress in the near term, with a rate rise expected in the days after the May 1 UK election whoever wins.
Alastair Stewart, a director at fund managment group Murray Johnstone, said it was hard to see any reasons for UK shares to make much progress without further gains on Wall Street.
"The major call for the UK markets is at what stage do you switch to overseas markets," Stewart said. "We can't go on appreciating for ever and we would expect a currency reaction in second quarter."

"Arguably there are signs of overheating in the retail market and parts of the housing market...the decision we are debating is when to switch to overseas assets and when to switch back to some of the exporting sector."

Among major overseas earners, Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was up 16p at 720-1/2, rebounding from recent underperformance, amid hopes for Thursday's first quarter earnings reports. Dean Witter upgraded the stock to a "buy."
A hesitant early showing on Wall Street helped pare London's gains by the close. The Dow was up two points as London closed, struggling to build on Tuesday's 173 point, 2.6 percent surge.
Other UK indexes also rose. The FTSE 250 index of mid-range shares was up 15.1 points at 4,528.4 and the Reuters-HSBC index of the leading 150 shares was up 10.69 points at 1,179.12.
Trading volume picked up from recently depressed levels to reach 805 million shares by 1557 GMT.
Banking group Alliance & Leicester was the most active stock for the third straight session, rising 12-1/2p to 545-1/2 in trade of 59.6 million shares.
Institutional funds were said to be hunting for Alliance shares they failed to pick up in the final auction of shares in the company, which made its market debut on Monday.

Publication of minutes of the last UK monetary policy meeting, which confirmed the Bank of England's call for higher interest rates, had little impact, as did the March retail sales report showing an in-line 0.3 percent increase.

Dealers were also reluctant to pay much heed to an opinion poll showing the ruling Conservatives, traditionally more friendly to business interests, sharply narrowing the opposition Labour party's lead.
Gilts were little changed by the close, with the long gilt future gaining just 3/32 to 109-1/2.
With European markets all benefiting from the latest Wall Street advance, the FTSE rose strongly from the outset and was up more than 50 points at its best.
Yet the 4,400 resistance point, last breached on March 14, proved a sticking point and the blue chip index was well below its day's peak by the close of business.
Chart analysts said a move through 4,400 level could be a trigger for further market gains, at least in the short term.
Bucking the positive trend in most of the market, drug group Zeneca fell 9-1/2p to 18.55 stg though dealers said the drop was due to little more than profit-taking after recent strength in the stock.

Schroders was among the day's biggest gainers, up 45p or 2.9 percent at 15.70 stg as strong markets sparked renewed interest in the recently-underperforming fund manager. Rival Mercury Asset Management rose 27p to 12.98 stg.
General Accident rose 22-1/2p to 833-1/2 after saying favourable winter conditions would see it reporting much improved first quarter results.
Outside the FTSE 100, Waverly Mining was the day's biggest casualty, tumbling 27 percent after closing its Monktonhall Colliery because of flooding.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
